correctness.rationale: For 1<h<3 the extreme vertices are the eight cube corners and six +/-h axis points. The determinant of any tetrahedron is multiaffine in its four points, so its absolute maximum reduces to 1001 vertex quadruples. Verified the actual standalone checker builds degree<=3 integer determinant polynomials and checks both signs of their gaps against five classwise envelopes in degree-3 Bernstein form on h=1+2s, s in [0,1]. Independently regenerated all 1001 determinants and EXACTLY 8008 nonnegative rational coefficients, with tight class counts 2,48,12,8,12 for 0..4 axial vertices. Comparing envelopes on (1,3) yields max{16,h²(h+3)}, with exactly two complementary cube maximizers and eight axis+opposite corner maximizers (ten at crossover r); independent pair comparison found no two maximal vertex tetrahedra sharing three vertices, and multiaffine convex combinations then exclude nonvertex optimizers. Cube volume 8, six pyramid extensions volume 8h on [1,2], and octahedron plus eight corner pyramids volume 4h² on [2,3], with 4h³/3 beyond; dividing determinant/6 gives five monotone branches, unique min 1/(3r). Boundary h=1,3 volumes match, but no equality-classification at those endpoints is asserted. This is an exact symbolic all-interval certificate combined with analytic vertex-reduction; not interpolation from numerical samples.

value.rationale: The cube–octahedron hull is a natural one-parameter transition including cube, rhombic dodecahedron and octahedron. Its exact largest-simplex occupancy and all equality types have a non-obvious algebraic switching point r<2 and unique worst ratio at a nonregular member, a motivated finite-dimensional extremal geometry result rather than an arbitrary slice.

final_claim: For P_h=conv([-1,1]^3 and six axis points +/-h e_i), the maximum contained tetrahedron determinant equals 16 for h<=r, h²(h+3) for r<=h<=3, and 2h³ for h>=3 where r²(r+3)=16. Its normalized maximum-volume ratio has a unique minimum 1/(3r), with complete maximizing tetrahedron classification for 1<h<3.
